A report on the impact of the 2021 UK–EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement,
three years on. Using monthly UK–EU trade data from January 2017 to December
2023, split before and after the TCA took effect in January 2021, we find
that the agreement has had a stifling effect on trade in both directions.

## Key findings

- UK **exports to the EU down 27%**; **imports from the EU down 32%**.
- The **variety of products exported down 33%**.
- Agrifood, textiles and clothing, and material-based manufacturing see the
  largest falls in both export value and product variety. Tobacco, railway and
  aircraft manufacturing are rare exceptions with gains in export variety.
- On the import side, value and variety fall in most sectors — especially
  agrifood, optical, textile and material-based manufacturing.
- The shifts appear **structural rather than short-term**, and are likely to
  persist without policy change.

## Policy recommendations

Mitigate the costs of the new arrangements, restructure UK supply chains
strategically, and help firms adapt to new barriers and raise productivity —
through sector-specific deals, engagement with individual member states,
lower non-tariff barriers, digitised customs, closer regulatory alignment,
and investment in port and customs infrastructure.

The report was cited in parliamentary questions.

**Report:** Centre for Business Prosperity, Aston University, 2024. With Jun
Du, Xingyi Liu and Yujie Shi. Also available as an SSRN working paper.
